correctness.rationale: Independently, choose a maximizer of |V_d| on the unit sphere with nonzero value; at a, ∇V_d(a)=λa with λ=dV_d(a)≠0 by constrained stationarity and Euler's identity. For any homogeneous H of degree m, the top derivation satisfies (D H)(a)=−λm H(a). Hence for a fixed i with a_i≠0 and m_j=1+j(d−2), (D^k x_i)(a)=a_i(−λ)^k∏_{j=0}^{k−1}m_j, never zero. In the full generator, lower homogeneous terms cannot reach degree m_j+d−2 at the next step, proving the exact degree by induction. This works also on the two-point sphere in one dimension, where every gradient is already radial. Strict degree growth proves independence. If fixed polynomial initialization and a constant matrix reproduced the trajectory via a linear projection, every kth derivative at zero would be a linear combination of the same finite collection of initial polynomials. The assumption holds for all real initial states, so these are polynomial identities; local existence suffices. For degree at most two the gradient is affine and the span including the constant is invariant. The radial strong-convexity example has Hessian (1+||x||²)I+2xxᵀ, so it genuinely lies outside common multi-equilibrium obstructions.
residual_risks: Existence of a fixed coordinate does not assert growth for every coordinate. The argument does not exclude nonpolynomial lifts or restrictions to special proper sets of initial states.

value.rationale: This supplies a quantitative, all-dimensions obstruction in a canonical dynamics class, not just one counterexample. Exact maximal degree growth gives a simple test for when a finite state-inclusive polynomial dictionary is impossible, even for a globally strongly convex single-equilibrium system. It complements, rather than restates, topological or conditional finite-dictionary criteria.
residual_risks: No quantitative approximation-error lower bound, no obstruction to arbitrary observables, and no global trajectory requirement.
